evidence.reason: The guard uses `relative(canonical, candidate).startsWith('..')` to decide whether the Git executable is outside the checkout. `path.relative('/work/repo', '/work/repo/..tools/git')` returns `..tools/git`, which begins with `..` but is not a parent-directory component; `..tools` is a normal directory inside the checkout. The code therefore accepts and executes a checkout-controlled executable when PATH includes such a directory, defeating the intended rejection of checkout executables. This is a routine implementation defect in existing intended behavior, not a new requirement; the smallest fix is a path-component check such as `rel === '..' || rel.startsWith('..' + sep)`.
